name: Kimberley (Big Hole)
note: 22.5 Mt excavated yielded 2722 kg (14.5 Mct), 1871-1914; pipe intrudes Karoo (Dwyka-Ecca) shale and dolerite

name: Kimberley pipes (De Beers, Dutoitspan, Bultfontein, Wesselton)
note: four neighbouring pipes mined since 1870s; merged as one body

name: Cullinan (Premier)
note: ~140 Mct produced since 1903 plus remaining resource (Petra Diamonds); source of the Cullinan diamond

name: Venetia
note: ~80 Mct produced plus underground reserve (De Beers)

name: Finsch
note: ~120 Mct produced since 1967 plus remaining

name: Jwaneng
note: ~450 Mct produced since 1982 plus ~250 Mct reserves (Debswana); under ~40 m of Kalahari sand

name: Orapa (AK1)
note: largest pipe of the Orapa field (118 ha) mined since 1971; intrudes Karoo basalt

name: Karowe (AK6)
note: low grade, very large stones (Lucara Diamond)

name: Letseng
note: lowest grade, highest value per carat (Gem Diamonds); Karoo basalt host

name: Catoca
note: fourth-largest kimberlite (66 ha), ~7 Mct/yr

name: Mbuji-Mayi (MIBA)
note: kimberlite field and eluvium, mostly industrial stones; the DRC is a top producer by carats (Kimberley Process)

name: Tshikapa alluvial diamonds (Kasai)
note: artisanal alluvial gravels of the Kasai and Tshikapa rivers; diamonds lie at the gravel-bedrock contact

name: Mwadui (Williamson)
note: 146 ha crater-facies kimberlite, ~20 Mct produced

name: Koidu kimberlites
note: small pipes and dykes

name: Kono and Tongo alluvial diamonds
note: alluvial gravels yielding most of Sierra Leone's ~55 Mct

name: Sperrgebiet coastal diamonds (Oranjemund)
note: raised-beach and marine gravels on the bedrock of Mining Area 1; diamonds trapped in bedrock gullies (Namdeb)

name: Elizabeth Bay
note: aeolian deflation deposits near Luderitz

name: Marange
note: diamondiferous Umkondo-age conglomerate and its eluvium; ~10-17 Mct/yr 2010-2012

name: Mir
note: first major Soviet pipe (1955); open pit to 525 m then underground; Cambrian-Ordovician carbonate host

name: Internatsionalnaya
note: small, very rich pipe near Mirny

name: Udachnaya
note: Alrosa's largest reserve; Cambrian-Ordovician carbonate host

name: Aikhal and Yubileynaya
note: Alakit-Markha field pipes

name: Nyurba and Botuobinskaya (Nakyn field)
note: Nakyn field

name: Lomonosov field (Arkhangelsk)
note: Arkhangelskaya and Karpinsky pipes; intrude Vendian-Paleozoic sediments

name: Argyle (AK1 lamproite)
note: ~865 Mct produced 1983-2020, mostly small brown stones and rare pinks (Rio Tinto)

name: Ekati (Panda-Koala-Misery-Fox)
note: ~75 Mct produced since 1998 from a field of small pipes; merged as one body

name: Diavik
note: ~140 Mct from four pipes under Lac de Gras (Rio Tinto)

name: Gahcho Kue
note: ~55 Mct reserve (De Beers and Mountain Province)

name: Majhgawan (Panna)
note: India's only producing diamond pipe (NMDC); Vindhyan host

name: Golconda diamonds (Kollur and the Krishna gravels)
note: the medieval and early-modern world's diamond source (Kollur mines on the Krishna); order of magnitude

name: Banganapalle conglomerate (Kurnool)
note: diamond-bearing Proterozoic conglomerate of the Kurnool Group worked in the Golconda era

name: Diamantina (Minas Gerais)
note: alluvials reworked from the Proterozoic Sopa-Brumadinho conglomerate; Brazil led world output 1725-1870

name: Chapada Diamantina (Lencois)
note: Tombador Formation conglomerates and their alluvials (Bahia)

name: Juina
note: alluvials around Cretaceous kimberlites

name: Muzo
note: calcite-pyrite veins in Lower Cretaceous black shale; the finest emeralds, worked since pre-Columbian times

name: Coscuez
note: western Colombian emerald belt

name: Chivor
note: eastern emerald belt; Muisca workings before 1537

name: Wadi Sikait (Mons Smaragdus)
note: Roman to medieval emerald mines of the Eastern Desert; the only emerald source of the medieval Old World west of Afghanistan

name: Habachtal
note: emerald in blackwall schist of the Habach Group (Hohe Tauern)

name: Panjshir (Darkhenj)
note: Panjshir valley emerald veins (USGS Major Deposits position)

name: Swat (Mingora)
note: emerald in talc-carbonate rock of the Indus suture

name: Sandawana
note: phlogopite schist emeralds

name: Kagem (Kafubu)
note: world's largest emerald mine; Gemfields grades of ~150-250 ct/t emerald and beryl in the reaction zone

name: Ural emerald mines (Malyshevo)
note: emerald-beryl-phenakite mica schists of the Izumrudnye Kopi belt (since 1830)

name: Carnaiba
note: Bahia schist-hosted emeralds

name: Sar-e-Sang
note: the lapis lazuli source of the ancient and medieval world (Badakhshan); lazurite lenses in Proterozoic marble

name: Malaya Bystraya
note: Baikal lapis lazuli in marble

name: Flor de los Andes (Ovalle)
note: Andean lapis lazuli in skarned limestone

name: Mogok marble rubies
note: ruby and red spinel in marble of the Mogok metamorphic belt; worked since at least the 6th century

name: Mogok gem gravels (byon)
note: gem gravels (byon) of the Mogok valleys; stones lie on the bedrock contact

name: Ratnapura gem gravels (illam)
note: illam gem gravels of the Kalu Ganga basin (Ratnapura), the Serendib sapphires known to medieval traders

name: Kashmir sapphire (Kudi Nala)
note: plagioclase pegmatite in marble near Soomjam, found 1881; tiny but legendary

name: Montepuez
note: secondary gravels over amphibolite; ~430 Mct resource (Gemfields)

name: Chanthaburi-Trat gem field
note: basalt-derived ruby and sapphire gravels

name: Jegdalek
note: ruby in marble (USGS Major Deposits position)

name: Luc Yen
note: ruby and spinel in marble and gravels

name: Mong Hsu
note: ruby in marble and gravels, found 1991

name: Ilakaka
note: sapphires in the Isalo sandstone paleoplacer and its gravels (since 1998)

name: Yogo Gulch
note: sapphire-bearing Eocene lamprophyre dike in Mississippian limestone

name: Naxos emery
note: emery (industrial corundum) lenses in marble, worked since antiquity; about 50 % corundum (block ungraded)

name: Milas-Mugla emery
note: Menderes massif emery in marble; about 50 % corundum (block ungraded)

name: Kuh-i-Lal (Badakhshan balas rubies)
note: the medieval 'balas ruby' mines described by Marco Polo; spinel in Proterozoic marble

name: Zabargad (St John's Island) peridot
note: peridot veins in mantle peridotite exhumed during Red Sea rifting; the ancient topazios and medieval peridot source

name: San Carlos peridot
note: peridotite xenoliths in Pliocene basalt flows; the largest peridot source today

name: Pyaung Gaung peridot
note: peridot in serpentinised dunite near Mogok

name: Sapat (Kohistan) peridot
note: peridot in dunite of the Kohistan arc

name: Aheim (Gusdal) dunite
note: world's largest olivine mine (refractory and slag-conditioner olivine); about 90 % olivine (block ungraded)

name: Bohemian pyrope (Trebenice-Podsedice)
note: Quaternary gravels with pyrope from Cenozoic diatremes; the Bohemian garnet worked since the Middle Ages

name: Gore Mountain and Ruby Mountain (Barton)
note: almandine megacrysts in Grenville amphibolite, industrial garnet; about 10 % garnet (block ungraded)

name: Merelani tsavorite
note: tsavorite (green grossular) in graphitic gneiss with tanzanite

name: Val Malenco demantoid
note: demantoid andradite in serpentinite

name: Outokumpu uvarovite
note: uvarovite on chromite-bearing skarns of the Outokumpu assemblage

name: Amelia (Rutherford mines) spessartine
note: spessartine in the Amelia pegmatites

name: Ouro Preto imperial topaz
note: imperial topaz in kaolinised veins in Proterozoic phyllite and dolomite

name: Schneckenstein
note: topaz rock crag mined for gems 1727-1800 (Saxon crown jewels)

name: Volyn pegmatites (Khoroshiv)
note: chamber pegmatites of the Korosten pluton with giant topaz and heliodor

name: Mursinka pegmatites
note: Ural gem pegmatites (Murzinka-Alabashka) worked since the 18th century

name: Katlang pink topaz
note: pink topaz veins in carbonate rock

name: Thomas Range topaz
note: topaz in cavities of Miocene rhyolite

name: Paraiba tourmaline (Sao Jose da Batalha)
note: cuprian tourmaline in pegmatite and quartzite

name: Eastern Brazilian pegmatite province (Governador Valadares-Teofilo Otoni)
note: the world's leading tourmaline and aquamarine pegmatite district

name: Pala and Mesa Grande pegmatites
note: Cretaceous gem pegmatites of San Diego County (Himalaya mine)

name: Oxford County pegmatites (Mount Mica)
note: Devonian-Permian gem pegmatites, first US gem mine (1821)

name: Elba pegmatites (San Piero in Campo)
note: Miocene Monte Capanne pegmatites

name: Nuristan pegmatites
note: Hindu Kush gem pegmatites (Kunar-Laghman)

name: Zschorlau (schorl)
note: tin-district granite with black tourmaline; the name schorl dates from the 14th-century Zschorlau mines

name: Sherlova Gora and Adun-Chilon
note: Transbaikal greisen aquamarine and topaz (Jurassic granite)

name: Shigar valley (Skardu)
note: Karakoram gem pegmatites

name: Wah Wah Mountains red beryl (Ruby-Violet)
note: the only commercial red beryl (bixbite) deposit, in Oligocene rhyolite

name: Namaqualand coastal diamonds (Kleinzee-Alexander Bay)
note: raised-beach gravels north of the Olifants River mined since 1926; diamonds on the bedrock footwall

name: Vaal River alluvial diamonds (Barkly West-Windsorton)
note: the 1867-1870 river diggings that began the South African diamond rush; terrace gravels along the Vaal

name: Jagersfontein
note: pipe in Karoo strata, ~9.6 Mct to 1971; Excelsior and Jubilee stones

name: Lunda Norte alluvial diamonds (Lucapa-Chitotolo)
note: Diamang's alluvial fields (1917-1975) and later concessions on the Chicapa-Luachimo-Chiumbe rivers

name: Cuango valley alluvial diamonds (Cafunfo)
note: high-value alluvial diamonds of the Cuango river

name: Akwatia (Birim) alluvial diamonds
note: Birim valley gravels (CAST/GCD since 1920s), Ghana's main source, mostly industrial stones

name: Carnot-Berberati alluvial diamonds
note: alluvials eroded from the Carnot sandstone (Cretaceous paleoplacer)
